correctness.rationale: PASS: Exact two observed-species sets have probabilities p^n, q^n, 1-p^n-q^n for singleton1, singleton2, both. Enumerating six unordered outcome categories yields J_n=1-p^n-q^n+p^{2n}+q^{2n}, not ratio of expectations. Delta1=2(pq)^2>0; Delta2=pq(-2(pq)^2+7pq-1), whose critical pq=(7-sqrt41)/4 gives stated p*. For dominant p beyond root rho of p³+p²=1, normalized H_n=Delta_n/(q p^n) strictly increases for all n>=2, by the factorized lower bound (1+p)p^4-(2p-1)=(p²+p-1)(p³+p-1)>0, and H_n→1, proving single trough. For smaller p each term in Delta_n positive. p→1 with n(p)=floor(log(1/2)/log p) yields J_n→3/4 while J2→1, sharp limiting drop 1/4. Polynomial continuity gives only stated finite multi-species inequalities for sufficiently small positive extra masses. Independent rational enumeration of 24 joint sample-set cases and exact sign/factor checks corroborates.

value.rationale: Expected Jaccard similarity of repeat communities is a standard ecological sampling-quality observable. Its strict sampling-effort monotonicity can fail even in the smallest nontrivial heterogeneous community; the sharp mass threshold, unique dip, and asymptotically 1/4 decline quantify a tangible bias not implied by pointwise observed richness. Multi-species continuity witness is appropriately limited.
